newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt takes formal delivery of U.S. frigates.
newsitem.headline: Egypt takes formal delivery of U.S. frigates.

text.p: Egypt formally received on Sunday two guided missile frigates from the United States and two more ships are expected to be delivered in 1998, as part of a package worth about $600 million.
State television showed Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak at a flag raising ceremony in Alexandria which marked the commissioning of the frigates, called Mubarak and Taba.
The U.S. embassy in Cairo said one of the ships was a grant to the Egyptian navy and the other was sold to Egypt for $47 million. They were transferred to Egypt in September, 1996.
The ships are armed with Harpoon anti-ship missiles, surface to air missiles, anti-submarine torpedoes and rapid fire guns, the embassy statement said.
Two more frigates have also been offered to the Egyptian navy and are expected to be transferred next year.
"The total transfer cost of the four frigates including ammunition, torpedoes, missiles and infrastructure improvements will be about $600 million," said the embassy statement.
The United States and Egypt hold joint naval exercises.
